newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: No ruling seen this week on Australia wage case.
newsitem.headline: No ruling seen this week on Australia wage case.

text.p: Australian Industrial Relations Commission (AIRC) sources said on Wednesday the tribunal would not hand down a ruling on the national "living wage" case this week.
"There won't be a decision this week," one source told Reuters.

Another source said AIRC president Deirdre O'Connor, who's presence would be necessary at the tabling of the ruling in Melbourne, would be in the west Australian city of Perth for the rest of the week.
The AIRC has said parties to the case will be given 24 hours advanced warning of a decision
The trade union movement has claimed a rise in all award wage levels of A$20 a week plus 8.75 percent, and then two further A$20 rises over the next two years.
The government, which has sought an A$8 weekly rise, has called the union claim irresponsible and the Reserve Bank has said the case could markedly affect Australia's ability to hold down inflation.
